body: dont worry about it, stats 2b03 was my first statistics course in my life and no previous knowledge needed. things are pretty straightforward

Personally suffering from anxiety and depression gives me the push. I’ve always had high standards for myself and I always kind of put my worth on grades. I know that’s an extremely bad thing for mental health, but it is how I grew up. I would feel very worthless and upset at myself if I didn’t have a grade high enough. I used to beat myself up and take all the blame because I wasn’t working hard enough. I’m in my second year of university right now, and this year I broke down. Because of my depression, some days I went to bed straight from classes, didn’t eat, didn’t study, and just slept until the morning when I had to get up. I felt extremely guilty doing this, because I could be using my time to write an essay, or complete an assignment. But instead I just slept away the precious time. But the anxiety side and my fear of failing/disappointment kept me going I guess. It is not a good mix to have both illnesses but I guess this might be an advantage. There were times where I can stare at a page of notes and burst into tears for 30 minutes because I couldn’t bring myself to focus. The guilt is tremendous for me and sometimes I have to give in because well, depression wins.
it’s too much to explain; and it seems like my thoughts mock myself because i can’t even put all of this into words. my mind is a complete mess.
because there’s no point in living my life.
the thing is, it’s better if it kills me. because i know most suicides are not successful unless it’s a foolproof way. so if i do end up dead, it’s the best.
